title: Fail-closed cross-repository Collision Assessor
goal: Guarantee that no Perfect Planner-managed worker can receive an edit claim until an independent read-only assessor has proven a complete, fresh, non-overlapping plan and resource snapshot and every approval has produced a durably delivered signal to its registered originating chat, with only ticket-scoped coordination remaining after discovery access is revoked.

meta.focus: one-time read-only global discovery, deterministic file and resource collision analysis, immutable clearance snapshots, transactional approval-to-chat wake-up, visible head-orchestrator and worker messaging, ticket-only walkie-talkie coordination, forced replanning, and fail-closed worker admission

spine.title: Guarantee and trust boundary
spine.summary: Define exactly what is guaranteed, isolate the assessor from orchestrators and workers, and fail closed outside the proven boundary.

spine.title: Global registry and one-time discovery
spine.summary: Build a machine-wide, read-only census with fresh identities, manifests, leases and a single-use capability that is destroyed after assessment.

spine.title: Deterministic collision proof
spine.summary: Normalize logical paths and resources, derive an immutable conflict graph, and issue a tamper-evident verdict only from complete inputs.

spine.title: Ticket coordination and claim enforcement
spine.summary: Turn conflicts into scoped walkie-talkie tickets, make approval wake its registered originating chat, and make every worker claim cryptographically dependent on both live assessor clearance and confirmed approval delivery.

spine.title: Operator visibility
spine.summary: Put a persistent head orchestrator and chat status above P1, keep every worker conversation visible, put the assessor first in the run flow, and make wait, replan, approval-delivery and decision states impossible to miss.

spine.title: Adversarial certification and rollout
spine.summary: Prove races, stale state, crashes, replay, path tricks and 100-planner load before packaging or calling the guarantee active.

vertebrae.title: Formal guarantee and threat model
vertebrae.notes: The guarantee covers Perfect Planner-managed workers because their edit claims are mediated. Unmanaged editors and arbitrary external processes cannot be prevented by this app; they must be detected by dirty-state and reconciliation gates. The document must never claim otherwise.

checklist.text: Specify the invariant: no managed worker claim exists without a fresh assessor clearance bound to the exact run, node, repository, branch, files and resources
Define the three separate authorities: assessor observes, head orchestrator decides, worker executes
Document fail-closed outcomes CLEAR, WAIT, REPLAN, USER_DECISION and UNKNOWN with no permissive default
Document the honest boundary for unmanaged tools, legacy Planners, offline repositories and incomplete configured-root coverage

vertebrae.title: Machine-wide Planner registry
vertebrae.notes: One process-safe registry per Windows user and machine. Every managed Planner must register before plan approval or worker admission. Records carry stable IDs, canonical repo/worktree/branch identity, plan/node manifests, leases, generation and freshness.

checklist.text: Persist versioned Planner registrations containing repository, worktree, branch, plan, node, files, resources, lease generation and heartbeat
Serialize concurrent register, heartbeat, update and unregister operations with an atomic process-safe lock
Treat stale, malformed, duplicate, partially written or unsupported registry records as UNKNOWN rather than absent
Record the configured discovery-root census and refuse completeness when any root or registered Planner cannot be accounted for

vertebrae.title: Single-use discovery capability
vertebrae.notes: Discovery is a one-shot capability issued to the assessor, never to the orchestrator or workers. It is bound to a run nonce, registry generation and short deadline. Assessment consumes and revokes it. Ticket operations use a separate narrow authority.

checklist.text: Issue a high-entropy, single-use discovery capability bound to run ID, registry generation, repository census and expiry
Atomically consume and revoke discovery access when the immutable assessment snapshot is created
Reject replay, expired capability, registry-generation drift and any discovery request after revocation
Expose only named assessor commands; provide no arbitrary path, shell, process-kill or general cross-repository read command

vertebrae.title: Read-only census collectors
vertebrae.notes: Replanned after RED review: board HTTP is display-only and is never an assessor authority. The native collector receives no caller-supplied path, root, URL, port or endpoint. Real collection runs once in a fixed internal child mode of the exact current executable, receives a nonce-bound bounded request through an anonymous stdin pipe, writes a bounded metadata-only response to stdout, and is killed then waited on at deadline so no privileged reader survives capability revocation. The helper reads only exact registry-addressed Planner metadata beneath configured roots, projects a strict DTO immediately, and the parent revalidates generation, digest, filesystem identity and observation time before acceptance. Missing, extra, duplicate, stale, aliased, timed-out or inconsistent input is UNKNOWN.

checklist.text: Collect every registered active Planner and configured-root manifest in a nonce-bound killable child process; timeout must kill and wait with zero surviving reader
Emit only bounded repository identity, branch, worktree, plan/node IDs, file/resource manifests, leases and freshness evidence; never raw plan, notes, proofs, refs, commands or source text
Return UNKNOWN when any registered Planner, configured root, manifest, generation, digest or filesystem identity is missing, stale, aliased or inconsistent
Prove the helper cannot escape configured roots, accept caller paths/endpoints, reuse a nonce, leak raw plan content or continue after kill/wait

vertebrae.title: Canonical path and resource identity
vertebrae.notes: The same logical repository file must collide across sibling worktrees and branches even when physical paths differ. Different repositories collide through declared resources such as database tables, ports, services and deployment targets.

checklist.text: Normalize Windows case, separators, dot segments, UNC paths, symlinks and junctions without permitting path escape
Derive a stable logical repository identity and repo-relative file key shared by all worktrees of that repository
Normalize resource keys for databases, schemas, APIs, ports, services, remotes and deployment targets
Fail closed on ambiguous globs, unresolved links, missing Git identity and resource keys without an accepted namespace

vertebrae.title: Deterministic collision graph
vertebrae.notes: The analyzer is a pure deterministic function over the B19 canonical claim snapshot. It never reads the filesystem, trusts caller paths or invents a disposition. Exact-file, directory-prefix and canonical resource collisions are evaluated from opaque typed keys. Glob claims are a hard UNKNOWN in v1. WAIT, REPLAN and USER_DECISION are emitted only when the frozen trusted disposition contract explicitly authorizes that result; missing or contradictory policy is UNKNOWN.

checklist.text: Intersect canonical exact-file keys, directory-tree segment prefixes and declared resource keys across every plan and active lease; reject every glob claim as UNKNOWN
Classify collisions as WAIT, REPLAN or USER_DECISION only from the trusted per-claim disposition and active-lease contract; otherwise return UNKNOWN
Generate stable conflict IDs and identical sorted output for identical census inputs regardless of discovery order
Refuse CLEAR when any participant, manifest, identity, freshness or configured-root coverage fact is uncertain

vertebrae.title: Immutable assessment and clearance
vertebrae.notes: Assessment artifacts are immutable and hash-chained. CLEAR issues a short-lived MAC-protected clearance bound to the snapshot hash and exact manifest. WAIT/REPLAN/UNKNOWN never issue clearance.

checklist.text: Persist the full census digest, registry generation, participant identities, conflicts, verdict, timestamp and expiry in an immutable snapshot
Hash-chain assessment, revocation, conflict-ticket and clearance events with torn-write recovery
Issue clearance only for CLEAR and bind it to snapshot hash, registry generation, run, node, manifest, fence and expiry
Reject modified snapshots, altered manifests, expired clearances, replayed clearances and any clearance from a prior registry generation

vertebrae.title: Conflict-ticket walkie-talkie broker
vertebrae.notes: After discovery revocation, orchestrators may only read and write tickets created by their own assessment. The broker exposes no plan enumeration or repository read path.

checklist.text: Create durable tickets naming both plan/node identities, exact colliding files/resources, snapshot hash and required disposition
Restrict each orchestrator to its own ticket IDs and reject arbitrary plan, repository or ticket enumeration
Deliver node-done, lease-released, manifest-changed, decision-required and replan-required events idempotently
Resume ticket delivery after restart without reopening global discovery or losing acknowledgement state

vertebrae.title: Assessor-gated worker admission
vertebrae.notes: This is the enforcement point that turns assessment into a guarantee. No scheduler or public command may create a claim unless the independent assessor atomically validates and consumes a clearance for that exact node manifest.

checklist.text: Require a live assessor clearance and confirmed approval-to-chat delivery receipt before every worker claim, including reassignment and retry
Atomically reserve the clearance manifest before returning a worker lease so two simultaneous claims cannot both win
Reject claims after registry generation changes, manifest expansion, clearance expiry, revocation or fence mismatch
Release reservations only after fenced completion, fenced failure, verified expiry or explicit ticket transition

vertebrae.title: Transactional approval-to-chat wake bridge
vertebrae.notes: The board may record a human click, but that alone never authorizes work. Every managed board must be bound to an explicit originating Codex task registration. The approval transition and its outbox message are idempotent, and worker admission stays blocked until a connector receipt proves delivery. Missing, disabled, dead-lettered or ambiguous routes are RED and visible; no thread ID is guessed from process or window state.

checklist.text: Bind each managed board instance to exactly one explicit originating-chat registration using plan path, plan ID, board process identity and a launch nonce without storing arbitrary prompt text
Route every approval entry point through one approval service that atomically records the approval transition and a durable chat-notification outbox record
Keep worker admission blocked while approval notification is UNROUTED, QUEUED, CLAIMED, retrying or DEAD LETTER and release it only after a matching delivery receipt
Make repeated clicks, watcher restarts, connector retries and app restarts produce one logical approval notification with preserved acknowledgement and receipt history
Use a fixed allowlisted approval notification template so plan text, worker notes and repository content cannot become executable chat instructions
Prove an APPROVE click reaches the exact registered Codex task, records a delivery receipt and wakes no other task; prove an unregistered route stays visibly blocked

vertebrae.title: Wait, replan and decision state machine
vertebrae.notes: The assessor reports facts and state transitions. It never edits plans or makes product decisions. The head orchestrator owns replanning, and material changes return to user approval.

checklist.text: Convert ordering-only collisions into durable dependency WAIT edges without granting a worker claim
Wake a waiting orchestrator on lease release and revalidate only the ticket-scoped facts without restoring global discovery
Force replanning when the blocker changed a manifest, contract, schema, API or other assumption used by the waiting plan
Require a new assessment snapshot and user approval after any material replan before claims resume

vertebrae.title: Assessor-first operator UI
vertebrae.notes: The first visible stage must be the assessor. It shows census completeness, snapshot hash, scan time, revocation proof and conflict tickets. It must never suggest CLEAR from a partial scan.

checklist.text: Display Collision Assessor as Step 0 before preflight with registry coverage, freshness and immutable snapshot identity
Display CLEAR, WAIT, REPLAN, USER DECISION and UNKNOWN with green reserved exclusively for proven CLEAR
Show each red-flag ticket with both plans, nodes, repositories, branches and exact colliding files/resources
Show global discovery as revoked after assessment while ticket-only walkie-talkie communication remains active
Trigger the single slowly rising alarm and direct chat notification for new decision-required or replan-required tickets

vertebrae.title: Head-orchestrator command deck and visible worker chat
vertebrae.notes: Reuse and harden the existing head-orchestrator strip and OrchestratorMessenger rather than creating a second messaging surface. The head is always above P1 for the active repository and plan. Messages are immutable, scoped, attributed and delivery-aware; a visual bubble never implies that a chat was actually notified.

checklist.text: Keep one distinctive head-orchestrator icon and identity card above P1 showing repository, plan, branch, lease, assessor verdict, approval delivery and current status
Show a persistent orchestrator chat-status box with inbox, outbox, unrouted, retrying, dead-letter and last-delivered counts without hiding failures
Give every visible worker a message badge that opens only that worker and node transcript with sender, receiver, correlation ID, timestamp, delivery state and acknowledgement
Prove worker-to-orchestrator notes and orchestrator-to-worker replies survive restart, remain append-only and cannot cross organization, repository, plan, node or worker boundaries
Let the orchestrator escalate an attributed worker message to the registered originating chat while displaying QUEUED through DELIVERED or DEAD LETTER truthfully
Capture the complete top-down visual: head orchestrator, live status chat, worker message bubbles, assessor Step 0 and P1 in one high-resolution proof

vertebrae.title: Adversarial native certification
vertebrae.notes: Tests must attack the guarantee rather than just exercise happy paths. Assertions may not be weakened to accommodate timing or Windows behavior.

checklist.text: Prove 100 simulated Planners with overlapping manifests never receive simultaneous conflicting claims
Prove simultaneous claim races, process restarts, partial writes and assessor crashes fail closed without lost reservations
Prove replayed tokens, stale generations, manifest expansion, symlink/junction tricks, case changes and path escapes are rejected
Prove incomplete registry coverage, unreachable boards and malformed records produce UNKNOWN and zero worker claims
Run at least 50 repeated high-contention certification loops on Windows with complete uniqueness and admission assertions

vertebrae.title: Browser and Tauri workflow proof
vertebrae.notes: Use isolated Chrome for repeatable automation and the packaged Tauri WebView2 for one native interaction pass. Evidence must include before/after screenshots, Git diff, console/network status and the exact conflict ticket shown.

checklist.text: Prove a clear census advances to preflight and visibly shows discovery revocation
Prove overlapping plans block claims, raise the red ticket and show both exact path owners
Prove lease release wakes the waiting orchestrator without reopening global discovery
Capture zero browser console errors, page errors, failed requests and unexpected HTTP failures
Capture one packaged Tauri WebView2 pass proving the native command permissions and assessor-first workflow

vertebrae.title: Fail-closed rollout and recovery
vertebrae.notes: Shadow observation may be used during development, but the guarantee is not active and no release may be called green until enforcement mode is mandatory, legacy/unregistered Planners block admission, and all certification evidence is attached.

checklist.text: Document migration from current board discovery and repository-scoped catalogues into the machine-wide registry
Make assessor absence, legacy unregistered Planner state and unsupported registry schema hard release blockers
Run formatting, full Rust suite, warnings-denied Clippy, TypeScript build, all browser E2E and packaged Tauri build
Record installer hashes, immutable assessment artifacts, recovery commands and all honest limitations in the handover trio
User confirms the displayed guarantee boundary, conflict workflow and recovery procedure before release is called complete

vertebrae.title: First-census registry and identity hardening
vertebrae.notes: Corrective vertebra created after the B04 RED review. It makes the first census possible without a prior census, binds it to a stable canonical digest, bounds every lifetime and configured-root count, and treats hardlinks, reparse aliases, SUBST/mapped-drive ambiguity and unresolvable filesystem identity as UNKNOWN. The guarantee explicitly names plan files plus the registry as authority; board HTTP remains untrusted display transport.

checklist.text: Expose a validated first-census snapshot and stable canonical input digest that excludes mutable timestamps and prior census output
Enforce maximum lease, heartbeat, census age, configured-root, registration, node, file and resource bounds including future-time rejection
Bind existing roots and plan files to Windows volume and file identity and fail UNKNOWN on hardlink, junction, symlink, SUBST, mapped-drive or reparse ambiguity
Prove concurrent registry mutation, first-census bootstrap, alias swaps and stale or malformed registrations never yield a complete census input

vertebrae.title: Single-use native metadata census API
vertebrae.notes: Corrective vertebra created after the B04 RED review. The named native command accepts only run ID plus capability token. It has no web/dev fallback and no caller-controlled path, root, URL, host, port, endpoint, shell or process argument. Capability validity and registry generation/digest are checked both before and after collection; every failure consumes or revokes the attempt and returns UNKNOWN.

checklist.text: Expose one named native census command whose request contains only run ID and single-use capability token
Revalidate capability expiry, registry generation and canonical census-input digest after collection before any snapshot can be accepted
Consume or revoke discovery on timeout, parse failure, metadata overrun, concurrent replay, generation drift or persistence failure

Prove the collect command, its collision-assessor permission and native call graph accept no arbitrary filesystem, board endpoint, browser, shell or process input; legacy board-discovery transport cannot satisfy census or admission

vertebrae.title: Canonical claim snapshot and disposition contract
vertebrae.notes: Corrective prerequisite created after B06 RED review. Native census code derives repository equality from the real linked-worktree .git metadata and a share-restricted handle to the resolved Git common directory; caller repository IDs and paths are never equality authority. It freezes opaque typed ExactFile, DirectoryTree and Resource claims plus machine-issued proposal/active lease, fence, dependency and per-claim disposition evidence before discovery is revoked. The native head orchestrator signs exact-scope authority receipts with an Ed25519 signing key that is never exposed to the census helper; the helper and restart path receive verification-only public authority plus an issuer epoch. Until the later trusted scheduler issuer is integrated, production issuance remains unreachable and therefore UNKNOWN. Issuer rotation invalidates old receipts without bricking registry recovery. Directory claims use logical segment-prefix ownership and include future children. Planned work remains visible; only terminal completed/released work leaves ownership. Cross-plan dependency identities remain globally scoped for B06 to resolve over the full census. Globs are deliberately unsupported in v1 and force UNKNOWN rather than a guessed expansion. Every typed claim, source manifest digest, physical alias edge and disposition is bound into the census/input digest.

checklist.text: Derive one opaque repository identity from real .git gitdir and commondir metadata plus a restricted Windows handle, and prove sibling worktrees converge while unrelated repositories do not
Project every file and resource declaration into a bounded typed ExactFile, DirectoryTree or Resource claim with canonical logical keys and physical alias evidence; every glob is UNKNOWN

Persist a trusted per-claim conflict disposition and active-node lease contract containing run, node, worker, fence, state, dependencies and assumption evidence; missing or contradictory policy is UNKNOWN

Verify machine-issued exact-scope authority receipts across the spawned census helper with a verification-only Ed25519 public key, reject injection/replay/rollback/illegal lifecycle transitions and rotate issuer epochs without recovery bricking

Bind sorted claims, alias edges, lease/disposition evidence and their source manifests into the attested census digest and reject any handle, inventory or manifest drift before persistence and on restart
Prove Git common-dir, hardlink, case, verbatim, UNC, SUBST, reparse, directory-boundary, resource-namespace, duplicate, permutation and glob-UNKNOWN adversarial cases
